label: prf:skein-mass-relation
title: Proof of $q$-Deformed Skein Relation
html:
The electron is the word \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 \in B_3, whose closure is the Hopf link (the trefoil 3_1 is kept as the backup reading). Neither closure has a hyperbolic complement, so the hyperbolic volume is 0 under either reading. The electron sits at the base of the topological tower, providing the unit against which all other masses are measured. The Higgs field is identified with the figure-eight knot 4_1 (cohomological embedding). Its algebraic quantum volume \mathrm{Vol}_q(\beta_{4_1}) τ-realises to the hyperbolic-volume constant \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) \approx 2.02988.

Applying the algebraic topological mass formula (algebraic topological mass) to the muon–electron ratio eliminates the overall mass scale. This gives m_\mu / m_e = \Phi_1(4_1) / \hbar_q^{2} at the \mathbb{Q}(q) level. Here, \Phi_1(4_1) = \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}(\mathrm{Vol}_q(4_1)) is the \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}-image of the algebraic quantum volume (Algebraic quantum volume \mathrm{Vol}_q(K)). Under \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}, the value \Phi_1(4_1) specialises to the numerical hyperbolic volume \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) via the volume conjecture [kashaev1997, murakami-murakami2001]. This constitutes τ-side naming of the algebraic value, not a derivation input. Substituting \hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1} and the CODATA value m_\mu / m_e \approx 206.7682827(46) yields

  \hbar_q^{2}
  = \frac{\mathrm{Vol}(4_1)}{m_\mu / m_e}
  = \frac{2.02988}{206.7683}
  \approx 0.009817,
  \qquad
  \hbar_q \approx 0.09908,

so 1/q = 1 - 0.09908 = 0.9009 and q \approx 1.10998.

The Skein relation acts as the mass-functional analogue of the Kauffman bracket recursion. At each crossing in the color-exchange diagram of a hadron, the three resolutions L_+, L_-, and L_0 satisfy q\mathcal{M}(L_+) - q^{-1}\mathcal{M}(L_-) = (q^{1/2}-q^{-1/2})\mathcal{M}(L_0). This relation descends from the q-deformed \mathrm{SU}(2) Chern--Simons functional on the 1-jet bundle prolongation of the CR manifold (Chapter). \square
